title: Garden shed, black shiplap potting shed (inferred from one photograph)

subject.summary: A long, low potting shed in black-stained horizontal shiplap, 5.85 x 2.40 m under a shallow mineral-felt roof, with two dark glazed lights, a full-height post between them and a ledged and braced door at the end the photograph cuts off.

sources.title: The owner's request: a construct of the shed in refs/photo-1.jpg, then a second version with a lean-to log store and a deck
Garden shed at Harlow Museum & Walled Gardens, Essex 01.jpg, by Acabashi, CC BY-SA 4.0
sources.ref: refs/photo-1.jpg, sha256 1802d1cd2c0e763427cd1468e10c02616363847b98462c258e7e770ad3d144d7, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Garden_shed_at_Harlow_Museum_%26_Walled_Gardens,_Essex_01.jpg (openly licensed stand-in for the owner's own photo)

facts.note: The photo's scale: 45 px between board shadow lines for a 145 mm shiplap board, cross-checked on the 55 px plant pots (~0.18 m) and the 140 px chair back (~0.45 m). Every size below is this scale read off the pixels; the boards' shadow lines, read row by row, are 53.5 px apart.
4.80 m of the long elevation from the frame's left edge to the right corner (1500 px at 313 px/m), plus a 1.05 m door bay beyond the cut edge where the photo ends.
Not measurable in a single frontal photo: a 2.40 m span, the usual depth of a shed with a 1.96 m eave and a felt roof this shallow.
588 px from the grass line at the wall foot to the fascia's underside, at 297 px/m: 1.98 m, made 2.00 m by 11 whole 175 mm board rows above the floor.
53.5 px between the boards' shadow lines, measured row by row down a clean stretch of wall at x 1000-1200, y 250-500; the boards are the 175 mm shiplap a shed of this age is clad in.
One more board row at the back wall (2.105 m) gives a 3.5 deg fall to the front, which matches the shallow felt slope the photo shows.
215 px between the outer beads of the right-hand light, 0.72 m.
294 px from head bead to sill bead, 0.99 m; set to five whole board rows (0.60 to 1.475 m) so the cut board ends land on the cladding joints and two rows stay above the head.
174 px from the wall foot up to the sill bead: 0.59 m, set on the third board row at 0.60 m.
The clear opening between the linings; a shed door is 0.76-0.84 m wide and the photo cuts the wall before this one.
The lower end of the 1.8-1.9 m a shed door is usually given, set so the head lining lands under the wall plate.
A 4x2 stud frame, the section a boarded shed of this age is framed in.
19 mm finished shiplap, read from the board edge at the right corner.
22 mm boards plus 4 mm felt, the build-up a shed roof has.
the felted edge the photo shows over the fascia, 40 mm rolled and a 200 mm deep fascia behind it.

annotations.text: Mineral felt over boarding, rolled over the eave (inferred)

identity.feature: shallow mineral felt roof, its edge rolled over the fascia
two dark single lights with a full-height post between them
black horizontal shiplap between corner posts, with a ledged door

authoring.provenance_note: One photograph, no measurements: every size is inferred at 313 px/m, set by the board pitch and cross-checked on the pots and the chair. The photographed elevation, its lights, posts, boards and felt are read from the photo; the door, the back wall, the frame and the roof's fall are designed; each part's note says which, and how its size and its shape are known.
next: measure the real shed if the owner can
check the roof's fall direction on site
